objective: Find the best evidenced execution architecture for the existing workload, prioritizing performance without considering implementation effort as a reason to reject a candidate.
authorization_boundary: Experimental files and isolated builds only. Do not change product sources, packaging, release tags, main, or public README until a repeatable material benefit and complete-output equivalence are established.
candidates: Current Python plus 22 C entry points (decision baseline)
Current pure Python backend (reference and diagnostic, not the decision baseline)
Rust replacing equivalent CPython-native loops at the same interface
Rust operating on a larger self-contained computation stage, evaluated separately from same-interface translation
JavaScript computation in Node, measured both inside Node and with actual Python integration costs
TypeScript as the JavaScript type/build layer, not a separate execution engine
Shell for orchestration; any claimed compute benefit must identify the actual external engine
immutable_behavior: Full public outputs except latency diagnostic fields
Database schema, SQL, candidate limits, ranking, stable order and scope isolation
Python Unicode code points including lone surrogates at supported helper interfaces
Normalization, exact source coordinates, page and session identifiers
Character and token budgets, cache state and result materialization
Dynamic overrides and fallback conditions for supported inputs
measurement_layers: Current complete-workload profile and actual call coverage
Equivalent pure computation kernels, with observable output consumption
Fresh and unchanged ingestion, direct recall, SDK stdio MCP, startup and RSS

formal_gate_draft.correctness: Zero complete-output, index, source-coordinate or invariant mismatches in all registered cases; any failure blocks adoption.
formal_gate_draft.benefit: At least 5 percent end-to-end improvement in a predeclared representative target, positive paired round-level confidence interval, and improvement in at least 5 of 6 balanced rounds.
formal_gate_draft.regressions: Retain every scenario and attempt. More than 3 percent repeatable regression in a key workload requires an explicit tradeoff decision; no silent cherry-picking.
formal_gate_draft.timing: Separate development/profiling from a frozen formal run. Serialize timed workers and use balanced orders. Resample rounds, not correlated individual calls.
formal_gate_draft.limits: A same-interface prototype cannot establish the best possible implementation of an entire language or a full-runtime rewrite. Conclusions must name the tested architecture and workloads.

persistence: Keep commits on the isolated validation/language-selection-20261117 branch with the user's existing Git identity; retain rejected prototypes and unfavorable measurements.
